sections.text: Perplexed by discordant thoughts, entangled in the snares of desire, infatuated by passion, they sink into the horrors of hell.
Self-conceited, stubborn, rich, proud and insolent, they make a display of their patronage, disregarding the rules of decency.
अहंकारं बलं दर्पं कामं क्रोधं च संश्रिताः।
Puffed up by power and inordinate conceit, swayed by lust and wrath, these wicked people hate Me Who am within them, as I am within all.

We had been discussing chapter 16, the Evasura Sampada Vibhaga Yoga. The divine and devilish qualities are the estates. This is the only estate you and I will carry with us when we die. All other estates will remain. But these qualities or tendencies of my mind, which are both as some divine tendencies and some devilish tendencies, I will carry that as my estates and Ill start from there. Youve seen so far that this divine tendencies will liberate me from my limitations.
The veilings on my mind which is right now is not letting me see the reality as is that myself and the supreme self is one and the same. On the other hand, the devilish qualities or the aspheric tendencies which in reality all it means is it binds me to this manifest world and therefore I will be more covered with ignorance from my own self. And therefore it is very important for me to understand what are these qualities. So in the beginning we have learnt about all the divine qualities and they are universal as we have said. So therefore there is not really much explanation needed. I should treat others just as I would like others to treat me.
Such divine qualities in if I practice it will liberate me from my limitations. But more and more I get bound to this world of manifestation. This is me and this is the world. This I want and this I want to avoid. It binds me more and more to this world. And therefore it is very important to understand how this thing works.
So we have seen so far that asuric tendencies make people believe that there is nothing more to this world than enjoy the sense gratification or satisfying the desires that I have, the lust that I have, and who knows, because I cannot see what was before my birth and I cannot see what was after my birth. Well, lets just consider this life is the only life that I have. And therefore lets make the most out of this life by by hook or crook. So I have now come to the conclusion that hoarding more and more wealth will make me happy. I will achieve that by any means, any unjust means. Even though I know this is not right, I will go ahead and do it anyway.
And once I get into that mode of mind, my situation would be that I will be constantly worried. Chintama Aparimayamcha AP Ill be overwhelmed by the worries. Im always worried about things which I dont have. Once I acquire it, Ill be always worried about how to safeguard it. Because just as I took it away from somebody, somebody will take it away from me. So this mode of mind will be constantly be engulfed by these worries.
But then at the same token my ego will start rising into its power and start thinking look, I have acquired this. These are the natural tendencies of my ego. Once I accomplish something, I start thinking nobody else could have done it but I did. The last few verses which we have seen describe this mode of mind. Even success is something that is very difficult to digest or to become worthy of, because success can intoxicate you with wrong thoughts.
Instead of getting you to a higher level by whatever you learned or achieved, it sometimes brings you down. And if you fall into that category, what happens is what we have seen in the last few verses, which basically says: Adhyah Abhijanavan Asmi -- I am rich. Once I have acquired wealth because I thought thats my security, that will give me happiness, I now forget why I acquired this wealth. It starts giving my ego a boost -- Look, I am rich. So now Im associating myself with my riches.
I start thinking I am my car, my car is me. I expand my identity not just to me as the body, mind and intellect, but now to all the possessions that I have. So my identity is incomplete without my possessions. Me minus my possessions is nothing. Now therefore I think: I am rich. Abhijanavan Asmi -- I am well-born. And Konyo Asti Sadrusho Maya -- Who is there who is like me?
These are the side effects of success. Success is something obviously very necessary for you to do what you need to do. But if that success only associate with why I wanted to achieve this then its not really that big of a problem. But when I start associating with my ego then all these side effects will kick in. So now what Im doing, even the thing which Im doing good instead of giving me good results give me actually wrong results. So Yakshe Dashyami Modishya I am making the sacrifice.
Sacrifice is something you make so that you become more humble. But now Im making sacrifice which makes me more arrogant. That look I am making sacrifice. Other people are not doing it. I am giving this donation. Donation is something is for you to get rid of more of your ego.
But it actually gives you boost your ego more that I am making donation. So the things which are supposed to be giving you the right results now start giving you the wrong results. Bhagavan said that this Asurik Sampath is. You need to be very careful in understanding that what are its evil effect on your mind and yourself. Once you are deluded. They get these wrong results even from the right actions.
Anek Chitta Vibranta Mohajal Samavrataha. Why all these things happening to them? Because they are Anek Chitta Vibhranta. They are bewildered by many fancy. They have all different kinds of fancies about what they are going to achieve, what their capabilities are. And I can also do that.
I tell all the time that if you are in one profession you always like to start thinking that something associated with it also I can do it. Most architects start getting into development and investment and real estate and all that. Because everybody comes to ask me how to do this. Why dont I do myself and also make money? In the end every architect who has tried has failed. Because thats not your really expertise or nature.
Youre good at something -- thats why you became something. But this fancy of mine which says, I can do this, I can also do this. I have achieved this, I can also accomplish this. Moha Jala Samavritah.
Because they are entangled into the snare of Moha delusion. This moha is simply my mind just cannot see the value of things and being as they are. So I start associating more and more values where they dont belong. Including on my own self, my own abilities. So Im completely entangled into it. Prasaktaha kama Bhageso.
We know how the addiction works. Once I get something, I want to get it again and again. My Starbucks example, first time I had the Starbucks coffee. Its not an addiction. The second time and a third time and after that, how can you live without it? Prasaktaha kama Bhagesha.
Once I start enjoying the sense gratification more and more I get addicted to it. Patanti Naraki Ashucha. These unclean minds, people with the unclean intentions, they fall into the Naraka hell. When things dont go right for us and we start worrying about it and start losing sleep over that. Its falling into hell. Other people may think you are doing very well but you ask yourself how you are doing.
Are you enjoying, Rajan? Because 18 things are going right in my life, but these two are not letting me enjoy those 18 things which are going right for me. So where am I living? Not in heaven, but in hell. From an outsiders perspective, I may be doing very well. Therefore you read these stories about people like the hedge fund manager.
Thered be billions, not even millions and still they are suffering through. He is under investigation, going to jail. If money was the only object which was going to make him happy, he wouldnt be living in this situation. Patanti Naraki Asuchao with that unclean intentions, pursuing the goals of satisfying their desires instead of giving them joy which they were seeking from those endeavors, they fall into this hell. Atma Sambhavitah Stabdaha. Now other people can see, but I think hes doing wrong.
Hes going to get hurt by this thing. But I dont see myself. Im suffering but Im still continuing. In Gujarat there is a saying, a gambler who is losing, he puts double the stake. He thinks the next time I can make it up. And this is really true.
Stock market, forget about gambling. Stock market people put money, the stocks go down. He think, oh now this is the time to get in. He puts more money into it. There was a company I was designing a headquarter in Charlottesville called Value America. I dont know any of you remember, but 2000, it was a rising company.
Internet bubble at the peak. And they hired me to design their headquarter in like June or July. And they had 600 people. And then they told me that by December we had thousand people. So they were designed with 1000 people. This building has to be completed by end of next year or so.
We are rushing to do that. And then just before the end of the year in December, I get a call and say, Rajan, send your invoice as quickly as possible because tomorrow the company may not be there. So anyway, the company was in a stock market. And then by the time I got involved, 15. And then when they called me it was about like $4 and say, got to be this good. No matter how much $4 will at least put $4,000.
I put thousand shares at $4, I said, I have seen that all the setup and those computers and all that is more than what they are saying. Well, the $4, then it eventually became 20 cents and eventually become zero. Even though I knew things are going down, I thought theres got to be a better deal. Thats because were atma Sambhavidah. Were overconfident about our own ability to think what reality is. Atma sambhavitah tab dhaha stubborn.
Everybody else says, I understand this thing better than you. Sabdaha dhanamanam adhan vitaha. Filled with pride and intoxication by their own achievement. No matter what the other people see what Im doing, which is dangerous, I dont say it myself. Yajante nama yagnehi te dambena Avidhi purvakam. I want to do right things.
I have done this thing because I think this will help me doing right thing. But I got completely distracted by my ego. It has affected my Ahankar so much that now when I am doing the right thing, as I said the sacrifice, Im doing it just in the name of it. Its not truly a sacrifice anymore. And Im doing everything else. Giving a donation, showing off what Im doing right for the community, services, all that.
Im doing it for the namesake only. If you dont put my name in this, Im not interested. I will be making a donation as long as you make me a board member. So my thinking has now gone completely in the wrong direction. I understood before, when I didnt have all this wealth, that all these yajnas and daan and sacrifice and services are for my own good -- to purify my own self.
But with all this achievement of my wealth, I have started thinking other way around. And therefore now Im doing all the things avidhi purvakam not in a right manner.

Verse 16 describes the state of being aneka-chitta-vibhrantah (bewildered by many fancies) and moha-jala-samavritah (entangled in the net of delusion). This is the scattered mind that chases multiple desires simultaneously, convinced that each new acquisition will finally bring fulfillment. The verse warns that such minds, addicted to sense pleasures (prasaktah kama-bhogashu), fall into naraka - not a place but a state of constant anxiety, dissatisfaction, and inner torment. Reflect honestly: How many fancies are you currently pursuing? How scattered is your mental energy? The teaching suggests that even worldly success, when pursued obsessively, becomes its own hell. Today, practice simplification: identify one desire you can release, one pursuit you can let go of, to reduce the chaos of competing wants.
Verse 17 reveals how even sacred acts become corrupted: the wealthy and proud (dhana-mana-madanvitah) perform sacrifices in name only (nama-yajnaih), motivated by ostentation (dambhena) and without proper understanding (avidhi-purvakam). Verse 18 identifies those who, filled with ego, power, arrogance, lust, and anger, actually hate the divine presence within themselves and others (mam atma-para-deheshu pradvisantah). This hatred of the Self manifests as disregard for ones own conscience and dismissal of others good intentions. Ask yourself: When has success made me more arrogant rather than more grateful? When have I ignored my inner voice because it conflicted with my desires? When have I dismissed good advice because it came from someone I felt superior to? These are the subtle ways we hate the divine within.
